As the orders grow in strength, King Philip will become nervous, and will eventually convince the pope to disband the orders, ending the game. The action in Crusaders: Thy Will Be Done is driven by a your personal action wheel, which you can upgrade over the course of the game. As you move your action tokens around your wheel, your options become more or less potent. Timing your actions and managing your action wheel will be the keys to success as you pursue your strategy. Turn Sequence Beginning with the start player and proceeding clockwise, players alternate taking turns. On your turn, choose between these options: A. Resolve an Action B. Upgrade a Wedge After you have completed your turn, the player to your left then follows the same process. A. Resolve an Action The left half of your player board contains the action wheel, which consists of six action wedges. Each action wedge begins the game displaying one of the five actions: Travel, Muster, Crusade, Influence and Build. Each of the actions has a different effect, but all resolve in the same way. 1. Count the number of action tokens on the wedge you are resolving. This number (X) is applied to the action. In general, the higher the value of (X), the more powerful the action will be. Other elements of your player board, such as troops and erected buildings, may add to the value of (X), depending on the action you have chosen. 2. Throughout the game, your action wedges may become upgraded. Upgraded action wedges allow you to split the action tokens in the bin as you choose between two different actions. You may assign all of the tokens in the wedge to only one of the actions, but in order to resolve an action at all, you must assign at least 1 token to that action. You may resolve the two actions in any order, but you must completely resolve one before starting the other. 3. After resolving the action, collect all the action tokens from the corresponding wedge and distribute them

[Rating: 1/10] Not a real strategy game , but not bad. 5/10 Anyway one star for weird province names and also offensive ones: it's not servia, it's Serbia!

[Rating: 1/10] Played on BGA.  + Rondel/mancala is the best / central feature of this Euro efficiency game.  It can be upgraded allowing for more powerful moves which are important in mid-late game. Managing action efficiency as pawns move around the rondel is its chief puzzle with some board positioning. – Mostly headsdown – Will feel very similar from play to play – Not a lot of depth

[Rating: 2/10] I strongly dislike the uncritical presentation of the Crusades here, though even if I didn't I would probably rate it as a 4 or so mechanically speaking. Nothing in the rondel or map expansion spoke to me strategically; the game feels as if the opportunity for cleverness in manipulating the game's levers ends up rather inconsequential to the final results, which wouldn't be a problem if this game were significantly lighter. [Rating: 2/10] This was one of the most dull, pre-baked games that I've played in a while. I felt like I was just going through the motions down isolated corridors where everything the gardens are all well-manicured. It's a shame because I do like the mancala mechanism as translated into a lighter game, however this is just another mostly solitaire engine building efficiency grind, and that ain't me.

[Rating: 2/10] The gameplay was relatively fun, but the theme is just terrible.  Each player is a crusader and you just go around wiping out all the people who live around there and claim to be doing it following God's will.  Ugghh!

[Rating: 3/10] Dry euro with an uncomfortable theme painted on top. The mechanics are fine, even nicely puzzly at times, even though concentrating on killing "heretics" seems the best way to go.

[Rating: 3.63/10] This game is decent visually, and its central rondel/Mancala mechanism is nice, but the game overall is too light. Its main strength is involving no luck and playing pretty quickly.  The Influence action is too powerful; an upcoming expansion addresses this.

[Rating: 4/10] :thumbsup: bonny bits  :thumbsdown: abated agency :thumbsdown: incidental interaction

[Rating: 4/10] Smart quick game with Mancala mechanics init. Race feeling (good).  Category: Filler+ (heavier family game)  ============  [GranieNaLuzie]

[Rating: 4/10] Crusaders: Thy Will Be Done is an action management and efficiency Euro that is driven by a simple yet engaging mancala-styled rondel and upgradable player boards. The game is very solitary. When interacting with other players, Crusaders only sees end-game majorities competition and the few times a player will claim a board space before another. This makes for a quiet play with little concern for others. Even though players are so insular focused, the puzzle on each player board is an impressive one. The rondel is easy to manage and always provides an option. On the few occasions there is not 

[Rating: 4/10] This game fell flat for me. The mechanisms just felt like a tedious exercise, despite the short play time. Also, the theme and mechanisms didn’t gel. As someone who enjoys Euros and abstracts, I thought I’d enjoy this. I can see why others would; it just wasn’t for me.

[Rating: 4/10] Very interesting game, with the largest descriptors being overproduced (euro-style cubes and meeples AND ameritrash minis), point salad, and rondel.  These together would normally be the end of the discussion (and my interest), yet here we are.  The point saladness felt good, with different strategic options changing the gameplay and making the game itself [b]fun[/b], which is the main takeaway.  The rondel is always a neat mechanic, and altogether, this was enjoyable.  Thinking about it, I'm not sure how much replayability the game has.  I would play it again 1-2 more times, but can't see it
